meta.title: Check your understanding: Cell technologies today

objectives: Describe how quartz becomes polysilicon, then an ingot, then a wafer
Explain why monocrystalline silicon won and how PERC, TOPCon, heterojunction and back-contact cells passivate their surfaces
Calculate the ideal refractive index and thickness of an anti-reflection coating

questions.prompt: Casting multicrystalline silicon is quicker and cheaper than pulling a single crystal. Why did monocrystalline silicon still win?
choices: Multicrystalline silicon has a band gap too wide for sunlight
Cast blocks could not be sliced into thin wafers
Pulling a single crystal skips the costly Siemens process
Grain boundaries trap carriers, and better cell designs gained much more on single crystals
questions.explain: The edges between grains are traps where electrons and holes recombine. For decades cheaper casting made up for that, but designs such as PERC gain much more on a single-crystal wafer, which tipped the balance from about 2018. Both kinds of wafer are silicon with the same band gap, and both start from polysilicon.

questions.prompt: An anti-reflection coating between air (n = 1) and silicon (n ≈ 3.5) should have a refractive index of √3.5 ≈ 1.87. How thick should it be to cancel reflection best at 700 nm?
questions.explain: The coating should be a quarter of the wavelength measured inside it: d = λ₀ ÷ (4 n₁) = 700 ÷ (4 × 1.87) ≈ 94 nm. Dividing 700 by 4 alone (175 nm) forgets that light has a shorter wavelength inside the coating than in air.

questions.prompt: Why do most silicon solar cells look dark blue?
choices: A thin anti-reflection coating cancels most reflection but still reflects a little blue
Pure crystalline silicon is naturally blue
Silicon absorbs blue light worst, so blue is what bounces back
Boron doping in the base gives the wafer a blue tint
questions.explain: Bare polished silicon reflects over 30 % of the light that hits it. The coating is a quarter wavelength thick for light near 600 nm, close to the peak of sunlight, so reflection there cancels while blue light is reflected a little, and that gives the colour.

questions.prompt: PERC (passivated emitter and rear cell), TOPCon (tunnel oxide passivated contact), heterojunction (HJT) and back-contact cells can all use the same kind of silicon wafer. What mainly sets them apart?
choices: The band gap of the silicon each one uses
Whether the wafer is pulled as one crystal or cast as many grains
How they treat and contact the wafer's surfaces, where most remaining losses are
How thick the wafer is, from a few microns up to a millimetre
questions.explain: A bare surface is full of broken bonds that swallow carriers, so the designs differ in how they passivate it and where the metal touches: small openings in PERC, a thin tunnel oxide in TOPCon, amorphous-silicon layers in HJT, every contact on the back in back-contact cells. The wafer underneath is the same.
